title: Drawer grids: Boss receipt
summary: For each row of drawers, produce the sum of that row. Empty rows contribute 0. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.
revisit: Earlier foundation work; the first unit establishes the prerequisite
descriptionMd:
The supply cabinet has uneven rows of drawers, including a few rows left entirely empty. Mina adds numbered weights to the final receipt at the unit's inspection desk. The first derived reading has weight one, so its position matters as much as its value.

For each row of drawers, produce the sum of that row. Empty rows contribute 0.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence.

Implement drawerGridsBossReceipt(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Nested array traversal. For each row of drawers, produce the sum of that row. Empty rows contribute 0. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys (earlier units are used while the first two levels establish the foundations).
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with nested array traversal. What state describes the portion you have already processed?
For each row of drawers, produce the sum of that row. Empty rows contribute 0. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.

Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. Use an accumulator and a one-based position counter, revisiting the first level's loop work.

cases.explanation: The derived sequence is [12,0,12,-2,22]. Its weighted products are [12,0,36,-8,110]. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 150.

The derived sequence is [6,0,-6,6]. Its weighted products are [6,0,-18,24]. Return the weighted sum of the derived sequence: multiply its first value by 1, its second by 2, and so on, then add the products. Return 0 for an empty sequence. This gives 12.
